schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE A (A1 INT, A2 INT);
CREATE TABLE B (B1 INT, B2 INT);
q1: SELECT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2, Y.B1 AS B1, Y.B2 AS B2 FROM A AS X, B AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.B1
q2: SELECT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2, X.B1 AS B1, X.B2 AS B2 FROM B AS X, A AS Y WHERE Y.A1 = X.B1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.A1 AS A1, X.A2 AS A2, Y.B1 AS B1, Y.B2 AS B2 FROM A AS X, B AS Y WHERE X.A1 = Y.B1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2, X.B1 AS B1, X.B2 AS B2 FROM B AS X, A AS Y WHERE Y.A1 = X.B1
counterexample: INSERT INTO A (A1, A2) VALUES (1, 2); INSERT INTO B (B1, B2) VALUES (1, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they join the tables A and B on different conditions and select different columns.
counterexample_dsp: The difference is in the join condition and the columns selected. Q1 joins on A.A1 = B.B1 and selects A.A1, A.A2, B.B1, B.B2. Q2 joins on B.A1 = A.B1 and selects B.A1, B.A2, A.B1, A.B2. A counterexample can be created where A.A1 = B.B1 but B.A1 <> A.B1.

q2_validation_sql: SELECT Y.A1 AS A1, Y.A2 AS A2, X.B1 AS B1, X.B2 AS B2 FROM B AS X, A AS Y WHERE Y.A1 = X.B1
